answer: The ledger counts names, not wishes, and every name on it has paid its own way. A name without Chartered shipwright hall oath is turned away at the counter, and an oath wrights swear before hull witnesses is the reason the counter can tell. Nobody is waved through free: an examination charge of £49, charged again each time a name fails is the price, and the garden never covers it twice. The clerk notes ferrous. bridge stays on the record.
